summary: Two Major core proof defects supported by explicit graph counterexamples: F1 boundary-only trip criteria omit closed straight trajectories; F2 a valid web needs two preparatory benzene moves, contradicting the immediate next-iteration reduction in Algorithm 7.1/Theorem 7.2. No counterexample to the principal web-basis theorem. A direct boundary-coverage invariant is verified for actual growth outputs. Current focused independent acceptance is recorded in independent_verification.

findings.location: Definitions 3.1/3.4 p.14; Definitions 3.14/3.16/3.19 pp.16–17; Proposition 3.21 p.18; Definition 3.30 p.22; Corollary 3.33 p.23; Section 5.8 p.62 and proof of Theorem 5.4 p.68.
findings.claim: The stated boundary-started trip criteria miss closed straight trajectories. Proposition 3.21's sufficiency and Corollary 3.33's literal monotonicity converse fail even for a connected graph with boundary.
evidence: Two internal vertices v black and w white, joined by three distinct simple parallel edges a,b,c; boundary edges pv and wq, p white and q black. Clockwise cyclic orders v=(p,a,b,c), w=(q,c,b,a). Every internal weighted degree is 4; graph connected, contracted, oscillating type (-1,+1).

Opposite pairings give the only physical boundary trip2 p-v-b-w-q and an invisible closed trajectory v-a-w-c-v. Orient v as source and w as sink; P1 holds and P2 is vacuous, but the underlying graph has 2-cycles and is not well oriented.

Trip1 walks p-v-c-w-b-v-a-w-q and q-w-c-v-b-w-a-v-p have their common-vertex set with the boundary trip2 occupy the entire walk, satisfying the written set-based consecutiveness condition. Definition 3.30 has no trip1 no-revisit clause.
Inverse-contract a to v-u-t-w with multiplicities 1,3,1. Together with b this creates a forbidden four-cycle, proving the original graph is not fully reduced.

Independent exact assistant-authored rotation-system check passed; certificate stored in verification/0120/counterexample_certificates.json. Actual source images verified by root and topology auxiliary.

findings.location: Definition 3.9 p.16; Algorithm 7.1 pp.71–72; Figures 43–45 and proof of Theorem 7.2 pp.72–73; dependency in Theorem 7.3 p.73 and Theorem 9.5 p.80.
findings.claim: The reduction algorithm's demand for a benzene move creating a forbidden square, and its claim of a square reduction on the immediately subsequent iteration, fail on a valid web.
evidence: Three-face strip Q=(q0,q1,q2,q3), H1=(q0,q1,a1,b1,b0,a0), H2=(b0,b1,c1,d1,d0,c0). Doubled internal edges q0a0,q1a1,b0c0,b1c1,d0d1. Doubled boundary leaves at q2,q3; simple leaves at a0,a1,c0,c1,d0,d1.
Bipartition black={q0,q2,a1,b0,c1,d0}, white={q1,q3,a0,b1,c0,d1}; boundary leaves opposite color. Every internal weighted degree 4, graph connected and contracted.
Complete simple-cycle lengths 4,6,6,8,10,12: only four-cycle Q, only six-cycles H1,H2. Q initially all simple; no Figure43 reduction or Figure44 loop deletion applies.

Initial face multiplicities Q=1111,H1=121112,H2=121212. H2 is the only initially flippable benzene face. After its flip Q=1111,H1=121212,H2=212121; no forbidden square exists. Flipping H1 next gives Q=2111, exposing the forbidden square.
Thus full reducedness fails by a two-move witness, but no one-benzene witness exists. The principal same-face term after the first benzene relation defeats the next-iteration reduction assertion.
Primary reviewer and two native auxiliary roles independently verified the graph/cycles/moves. Assistant-authored exact graph certificate passed all assertions; no author code executed.
assumptions_verified: Every internal vertex is incident to one doubled edge, so there is no contraction removing the obstruction.
An oscillating example follows by splitting the two doubled boundary leaves.
Actual Figure43 requires a non-simple square side; Q initially has none.
findings.core_dependency: Theorem 7.2's termination proof; alternative basis spanning in Theorem 7.3; written semistandard spanning in Theorem 9.5. Principal Sections 5–6 basis proof is separate.
findings.repair: Specify and justify a finite preparatory witness sequence and a well-founded recursive measure controlling face number, progress along the witness, and lower-face skein side terms. Arbitrary benzene moves can undo the first flip. A general corrected reduction schedule is not proved by this review.
findings.consequence: Actual one-step/termination proof defect; no counterexample to the principal web-basis conclusion.
findings.classification_basis: Concrete counterexample to an asserted algorithmic step in a core proof and its alternate basis argument; Major under the original rubric.

checks.reason: Two internal vertices v,w joined by three distinct simple edges a,b,c with boundary legs p,q and cyclic orders v=(p,a,b,c),w=(q,c,b,a) are a connected bipartite weighted-degree4 graph. Parallel distinct edges are allowed before full reducedness. Opposite-edge pairings give boundary strand p-v-b-w-q and closed straight trajectory v-a-w-c-v. Definition3.16 starts trips at boundary vertices, so the latter is not tested. Orienting v as source,w as sink is permitted. The sole physical boundary strand is simple, while pairwise triple conditions are vacuous; the graph nevertheless has2-cycles, directly failing Definition3.19. Excluding isolated components does not repair this example.

The two trip1 walks in the report revisit v,w but every vertex along each belongs to its intersection with the boundary trip2 vertex set. Under Definition3.30's literal set-based consecutiveness condition, these intersections are consecutive; a no-revisit condition is printed for trip2, not for trip1. Expanding a by the inverse contraction into multiplicities1,3,1 and using b yields a forbidden4-cycle. The report correctly keeps the literal-reading qualification, rather than assuming any possible unstated stronger predicate.
